title: I built a system that turns a text prompt into a complete procedural house
author: PlanktonOver9648
selftext:
**The model itself**  
An off-the-shelf sentence encoder (bge-base-en-v1.5) reads the prompt.  
A small transformer decoder I trained from scratch (6 layers, \~17M parameters) writes the action sequence. Its vocabulary is about 6,000 action tokens.  
Decoding is constrained: at each step the model can only pick tokens the engine's schema allows there, so it can't write an invalid recipe.  
Training data comes from the engine itself. It generates and validates buildings, the training loop scores the model's answers by actually building them, and the misses are replayed. The latest run was 9 hours on an RTX 5070.  
Inference runs in plain C++ inside the app (no Python, no ONNX), and I check it against the PyTorch model token for token.  
**Checking that it did what you asked**  
A rule-based reader pulls the requirements out of your sentence ("stone walls", "3 bedrooms", "a moat", "booths"). The app checks each one on the finished building, and those are the ticks you see in the video. If the model misses something, the requirement gets written into its actions and the building is rebuilt. Only an honest "met / not met" is shown.  
**What's new in 1.2**  
castles (keep, wings, round or square towers, moat), round or square malls with a food court, pubs, shops, flats over shops, warehouses, 13 house styles  
change a building in words: "make the towers round with cone roofs" changes only the towers, in about 0.1 s  
variants: "3 more like this" for the same sentence  
walk through the building in first person  
whole towns from one sentence ("a village with a castle, two pubs and twelve houses")  
export to Unreal and Unity (FBX with colliders), Godot (GLB with physics), Blender (plus an add-on) or CAD (DXF plans)  
**What it can't do yet**  
The vocabulary is fixed by the engine, so it can only build what the engine knows; ask for a lighthouse and you won't get one. The next model will be bigger, and it waits for new engine features first: ruined and damaged buildings, Hong Kong–style megablocks and cyberpunk towers.  
I'm happy to go deeper on the training loop, the constrained decoding or the requirement checks if anyone's interested. It's a one-person project, released on Patreon
